doc_description: CVS Health Corporation’s Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2022 details its integrated retail/pharmacy benefits/insurance model (9,000+ stores, 110M+ PBM members, ~35M insured) and $322.5B of revenue, records a $5.3B opioid litigation charge and a $2.5B Omnicare LTC held‑for‑sale write‑down, notes divestitures of PayFlex and bswift plus pending acquisitions of Signify Health and Oak Street Health, highlights COVID‑19 activity (15M+ tests, ~28M vaccines), and outlines regulatory risks including Medicare Star Ratings pressure and heightened PBM/health plan oversight.

structure.title: Preface
structure.summary:
- Filing overview: CVS Health Corporation’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022; Commission File No. 001-01011; incorporated in Delaware; principal office in Woonsocket, RI; common stock traded on NYSE under “CVS.”
- Registrant status and compliance: Well-known seasoned issuer; large accelerated filer; not a shell company; timely filing and Interactive Data File compliance; auditor attestation of internal control over financial reporting (SOX 404(b)); no error corrections/restatements indicated.
- Capital and market data: Aggregate market value of non-affiliate common stock as of June 30, 2022 approximately $121.3 billion; 1,284,111,667 shares outstanding as of February 1, 2023.
- Incorporation by reference: 2023 Proxy Statement incorporated into Parts III and IV.
- Table of Contents highlights: Standard Part I–IV sections including Business, Risk Factors, Properties, Legal Proceedings, Market for Common Equity, MD&A, Market Risk, Financial Statements, Controls and Procedures, and auditor/inspection disclosures.
- Forward-looking statements: Safe harbor under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act; cautionary language covering outlook, strategy, operating metrics, regulatory impacts, and potential acquisitions (including Oak Street Health and Signify Health), integration risks, leverage, cash flows, and other uncertainties; no obligation to update.
- Business overview: CVS Health as a diversified health solutions company with an integrated model aimed at improving access, outcomes, and lowering costs; footprint includes 9,000+ retail locations, 1,100+ walk-in clinics, a leading PBM with 110M+ plan members and specialty pharmacy, long-term care pharmacy, and health insurance serving ~35M people (including Medicare Advantage and leading standalone Part D plan).
- Reportable segments: Health Care Benefits, Pharmacy Services, Retail/LTC, and Corporate/Other.
- Strategy: Consumer-centric transformation to deliver personalized, simpler, and increasingly digital health solutions; shift from transaction-based to holistic health (physical, emotional, social, economic); expansion into next-generation care delivery and health services to drive long-term growth and stakeholder value.
- COVID-19 response and impact: Extensive national role in testing and vaccination; as of 12/31/22 testing at 4,700+ locations and community sites; ReturnReady solution; vaccines offered at 9,000+ locations; in 2022 administered 15M+ tests, nearly 28M vaccines, and sold 63M+ OTC test kits; continued focus on equity in access; impacts discussed throughout the filing.
- Segment detail (beginning): Health Care Benefits segment described as a leading diversified benefits provider serving ~35M people with tools to support informed care decisions and a broad range of traditional, voluntary, and consumer-directed insurance products (section continues beyond the excerpt).

structure.title: Business
structure.heading: Item 1: Business
structure.start_phrase:
CVS Health Corporation, together with its subsidiaries (collectively, “CVS Health,” the “Company,” “we,” “our” or “us”), is a leading diversified health
solutions company reshaping health care to help make healthier happen for more Americans.
structure.summary:
- Scope: Part I, Item 1 (Business) of CVS Health’s Form 10-K.

- Company overview: CVS Health is a diversified health solutions company integrating care delivery, pharmacy, and health insurance. It operates 9,000+ retail locations, 1,100+ walk-in clinics, a leading PBM with 110M+ plan members, specialty pharmacy solutions, and a senior pharmacy care business serving 1M+ patients annually. Through its Health Care Benefits business, it serves an estimated 35M people across traditional, voluntary, and consumer-directed plans, including Medicare Advantage and a leading standalone Medicare Part D PDP. The integrated model is intended to improve access and outcomes while lowering costs.

- Reportable segments: Health Care Benefits, Pharmacy Services, Retail/LTC, and Corporate/Other.

- Business strategy: Reimagine a consumer-centric healthcare experience that is more personalized, simple, and digital, enabling care when/where/how consumers prefer. Shift from transaction-based care to holistic health (physical, emotional, social, economic). Expand into next-generation care delivery and health services to increase provider and consumer satisfaction and drive sustainable long-term growth and stakeholder value.

- COVID-19 response: Significant national role leveraging local presence and scale. As of December 31, 2022, CVS offered diagnostic testing at 4,700+ pharmacy locations and community sites and via ReturnReady; sold OTC test kits in stores and online; administered vaccinations in long-term care facilities (since Dec 2020) and retail pharmacies (since Feb 2021), including boosters and pediatric doses. In 2022, it conducted 15M+ tests, administered nearly 28M vaccines, and sold 63M+ OTC test kits. Ongoing commitment to testing/vaccine equity through optimized site locations and targeted outreach. Broader COVID-19 impacts are discussed throughout the 10-K.

- Health Care Benefits segment overview: One of the nation’s leading diversified health benefits providers, serving ~35M people, offering tools and resources to help members make informed healthcare decisions and a broad suite of traditional, voluntary, and consumer-directed insurance products.

nodes.title: Health Care Benefits Segment
nodes.heading: 4 Health Care Benefits Segment
nodes.start_phrase: The Health Care Benefits segment operates as one of the nation’s leading diversified health care benefits providers, serving an estimated 35 million people as of December 31, 2022.
nodes.summary:
- Company overview: CVS Health is a diversified health solutions company with an integrated model spanning retail pharmacies (9,000+ locations), walk-in clinics (1,100+), a leading PBM (110M+ members, specialty and senior pharmacy care), and health insurance serving ~35M people, including Medicare Advantage and Part D.
- Reportable segments: Health Care Benefits, Pharmacy Services, Retail/LTC, and Corporate/Other.
- Strategy: Reimagining consumer healthcare with personalized, simpler, increasingly digital solutions; shifting from transaction-based to holistic health (physical, emotional, social, economic); expanding next-generation care delivery and health services to improve outcomes, reduce costs, and drive long-term growth.
- COVID-19 response: Large-scale testing (4,700+ locations and community sites), Return Ready solution, OTC test kit sales; vaccination programs in long-term care and retail pharmacies, including boosters and pediatric doses. In 2022: 15M+ tests administered, ~28M vaccines, and 63M+ OTC test kits sold; continued focus on equitable access and ongoing role in testing/vaccination.
- Health Care Benefits segment scope: Serves ~35M people (as of 12/31/22) with medical, pharmacy, dental, behavioral health, medical management, Medicare Advantage, Medicare Supplement, PDP, Medicaid management, and HIT products/services; workers’ compensation business sold in 2020.
- Customers: Employer groups (large, mid, small), individuals, students, part-time/hourly workers, health plans, providers, government entities, labor groups, and expatriates.
- Insurance vs. administrative services: “Insured” products (Company assumes risk) vs. “ASC” products (sponsor assumes risk); medical stop-loss offered for self-insured employers.
- Commercial medical offerings: POS, PPO, HMO, Indemnity; HSAs and consumer-directed plans; Aetna Virtual Primary Care launched in 2021 with access to virtual and in-person care (including MinuteClinic); complementary offerings include dental, behavioral health, EAP, provider network access, and vision.
- Government medical programs:
  - Medicare Advantage: HMO/PPO plans with enhanced benefits vs. Original Medicare; offered in 46 states + DC (2022); national PPO for employer groups; integrated medical + pharmacy when combined with PDP.
  - Medicare PDP: National Part D prescription drug plans offered in all 50 states + DC (2022).
  - Medicare Supplement: Plans covering Medicare cost gaps offered in 49 states + DC (2022).
  - Medicaid and CHIP: Insured or ASC services under state contracts in 16 states (2022).
  - Duals (Medicare-Medicaid): Coordinated coverage for dually eligible members, managing 100% of care and providing additional services as needed.

nodes.title: Health Care Benefits Segment - Introduction
nodes.heading: 4 Health Care Benefits Segment
nodes.start_phrase: The Health Care Benefits segment operates as one of the nation’s leading diversified health care benefits providers, serving an estimated 35 million people as of December 31, 2022.
nodes.summary: Introduces the Health Care Benefits segment as a leading diversified health care benefits provider serving an estimated 35 million people as of December 31, 2022, supporting members and their health care professionals with information and resources for informed decisions. Describes a broad portfolio of traditional, voluntary, and consumer-directed health insurance products and related services, including medical, pharmacy, dental, behavioral health plans, medical management, Medicare Advantage, Medicare Supplement, PDPs, Medicaid health care management services, and health information technology products and services. Notes prior provision of workers’ compensation administrative services through the Coventry Health Care Workers’ Compensation business, sold on July 31, 2020. Identifies customers as employer groups, individuals, college students, part-time and hourly workers, health plans, providers, governmental units and government-sponsored plans, labor groups, and expatriates.

nodes.title: Health Care Benefits Products and Services
nodes.heading: 4.1 Health Care Benefits Products and Services
nodes.start_phrase: The Company refers to insurance products (where it assumes all or a majority of the risk for medical and dental care costs) as “Insured” and administrative services contract products (where the plan sponsor assumes all or a majority of the risk of medical and dental care costs) as “ASC.”
nodes.summary:
- Scope of Health Care Benefits segment: Offers medical, pharmacy, dental, and behavioral health plans; medical management; Medicare Advantage, Medicare Supplement, and Part D (PDP); Medicaid health care management; and health information technology products and services. Provided workers’ compensation administrative services until divested on July 31, 2020. Customers include employers of all sizes, individuals, students, part-time/hourly workers, health plans, providers, government units and programs, labor groups, and expatriates.
- Product model definitions: “Insured” (Company assumes risk) vs. “Administrative services contract” (ASC) where plan sponsors assume most risk.
- Commercial Medical offerings: POS, PPO, HMO, Indemnity; HSAs and consumer-directed plans; Aetna Virtual Primary Care (launched 2021) pairing virtual care with in-network in-person options including MinuteClinic; medical stop-loss insurance for self-insured employers; complementary products such as dental, behavioral health/EAP, vision, and provider network access.
- Government Medical programs:
  - Medicare Advantage: HMO/PPO plans with enhanced benefits vs. Original Medicare; offered in 46 states and D.C. in 2022; national PPOs for qualifying employer groups; integrated employer product when combined with PDP.
  - Medicare PDP: National Part D prescription coverage offered in all 50 states and D.C. in 2022.
  - Medicare Supplement: Plans covering gaps in Original Medicare, available in 49 states and D.C. in 2022.
  - Medicaid and CHIP: Insured or ASC services in 16 states in 2022 under multi‑year, annually appropriated contracts.
  - Duals: Integrated coverage and care coordination for members eligible for both Medicare and Medicaid.
- Transformative health solutions: Portfolio aimed at holistic, integrated health and wellness, enhancing Commercial and Government offerings with innovative, integrated experiences and care enablement.
- Provider networks and affordability: Contracts with physicians, hospitals, and other facilities; use of utilization management, risk-sharing arrangements, clinical guidelines, and provider performance data to improve quality and affordability. Nationwide network of approximately 1.6 million participating providers, including labs, imaging, urgent care, and other freestanding facilities (as of December 31, 2022).
- Quality and accreditation:
  - CMS Star Ratings used to assess Medicare plan quality and member experience.
  - NCQA accreditation for Aetna HMO plans; Aetna Life Insurance Company (ALIC) holds nationwide NCQA PPO accreditation; as of December 31, 2022, all eligible Commercial HMO and ALIC PPO members were in NCQA‑accredited plans.
  - Credentialing and re-credentialing aligned with NCQA, URAC, and state/federal standards; NCQA CVO certification and URAC CVO accreditation.
  - Ongoing quality measurement, improvement programs, and analytics offered to providers and purchasers.
- Information systems and technology: End‑to‑end IT platforms for engagement, enrollment, benefits administration, care management, operations, and analytics, connected via real‑time integration layers. Continued investment in enterprise data platforms, cloud, digital/mobile experiences, and emerging technologies (voice, AI, robotics) to automate, reduce costs, and improve member experience by guiding members through their health care journey.

nodes.title: Health Care Benefits Provider Networks
nodes.heading: 4.2 Health Care Benefits Provider Networks
nodes.start_phrase: The Company contracts with physicians, hospitals and other providers for services they provide to the Company’s members.
nodes.summary: The excerpt outlines the company’s integrated health and wellness strategy and its Health Care Benefits infrastructure. It highlights a broad portfolio of transformative products and services designed to complement Commercial and Government medical offerings and enhance care delivery. The company maintains a nationwide provider network of roughly 1.6 million participating physicians, hospitals, and ancillary facilities (labs, imaging, urgent care), supported by negotiated reimbursement rates, risk‑sharing arrangements, utilization management guidelines, and data sharing to promote quality and affordability. Quality oversight includes alignment with CMS’s Medicare Star Ratings, pursuit of NCQA accreditation for Aetna HMO plans and nationwide NCQA PPO accreditation for Aetna Life Insurance Company, and adherence to NCQA/URAC standards for provider selection, credentialing, and CVO certification; hospitals are required to hold CMS certification or accreditation from recognized bodies. The company also delivers quality measurement, improvement programs, and analytics to providers and purchasers. Its information systems comprise end‑to‑end platforms for member engagement, enrollment, benefit administration, care management, service operations, financial reporting, and analytics, integrated for real‑time data exchange. Ongoing investments focus on enterprise data platforms, cloud, and digital channels, as well as emerging technologies such as voice, artificial intelligence, and robotics to automate processes, reduce costs, and improve member experience.

nodes.title: Health Care Benefits Quality Assessment
nodes.heading: 4.3 Health Care Benefits Quality Assessment
nodes.start_phrase: CMS uses a 5-star rating system to monitor Medicare health care and drug plans and ensure that they meet CMS’s quality standards.
nodes.summary:
- Describes a portfolio of transformative products and services designed to deliver holistic, integrated health and wellness solutions that complement Commercial Medical and Government Medical offerings, enhancing care delivery and member experience.
- Details the Health Care Benefits provider networks, including contracting with physicians, hospitals, and ancillary providers; employing utilization management, risk-sharing arrangements, clinical guidelines, and provider data sharing to improve quality and affordability; network size of approximately 1.6 million participating providers as of December 31, 2022, including labs, imaging, urgent care, and freestanding facilities.
- Explains quality assessment through CMS’s 5-star rating system for Medicare plans, covering preventive care, chronic disease management, and customer satisfaction, with implications for plan comparison and pricing.
- Outlines accreditations: NCQA accreditation for Aetna HMO plans and nationwide NCQA PPO accreditation for Aetna Life Insurance Company (ALIC); as of December 31, 2022, all eligible Commercial HMO and ALIC PPO members participated in NCQA-accredited plans.
- Describes provider selection and credentialing aligned with NCQA, URAC, and regulatory standards; Company holds NCQA CVO certification (all options) and URAC CVO accreditation; practitioners’ credentials are verified and participating hospitals must be CMS-certified or accredited by recognized bodies (The Joint Commission, AOA, DNV).
- Highlights quality and outcomes initiatives, including quality improvement programs and health care data analytics offered to providers and purchasers.
- Summarizes Health Care Benefits information systems: end-to-end platforms for member engagement, enrollment, benefits administration, care management, service operations, and financial analytics; integrated via real-time data layers; ongoing investments in enterprise data platforms, cloud, digital products, and emerging technologies (voice, AI, robotics) to automate, reduce costs, and improve mobile/web member experiences.

nodes.title: Health Care Benefits Information Systems
nodes.heading: 4.4 Health Care Benefits Information Systems
nodes.start_phrase: The Health Care Benefits segment currently operates and supports an end-to-end suite of information technology platforms to support member engagement, enrollment, health benefit administration, care management, service operations, financial reporting and analytics.
nodes.summary:
- Portfolio focus: Transformative, integrated products and services designed to improve individual health and wellness, complementing Commercial and Government Medical offerings and enabling enhanced, holistic care delivery.
- Provider networks and utilization: Contracts with physicians, hospitals, and ancillary providers using negotiated rates, risk-sharing arrangements, utilization guidelines, and data sharing to promote appropriate use and affordability; approximately 1.6 million participating providers nationwide as of December 31, 2022.
- Quality and accreditation: Emphasis on CMS Medicare Star Ratings for plan quality and member experience; broad NCQA accreditations (Aetna HMO plans and ALIC nationwide PPO) with Commercial HMO and ALIC PPO members in accredited plans; credentialing aligned with NCQA/URAC and regulatory standards; NCQA and URAC CVO certifications; hospital participation contingent on CMS certification or major accrediting bodies.
- Provider quality programs: Ongoing quality/outcome measurement, improvement initiatives, and analytics offered to providers and purchasers.
- Information systems: End-to-end technology platforms supporting engagement, enrollment, benefits administration, care management, operations, and analytics; integrated real-time data layer; investments in cloud, enterprise data platforms, digital/mobile, voice, AI, and robotics to automate, reduce cost, and improve experiences and outcomes.
- Customer base and products: Broad U.S. footprint with some international members; offers traditional, voluntary, and consumer-directed plans to employers, individuals, students, part-time/hourly workers, health plans, providers, government units, labor groups, and expatriates; Medicare (individual and group retirees), Medicaid, CHIP, and dual-eligible coverage.
- Distribution and marketing: Sold via company sales, brokers/agents/consultants, Private Exchanges, and Public Exchanges; supports commissions/fees and facilitates broker compensation where applicable; entered ACA Public Exchanges in 8 states in 2022 and 4 more in 2023; uses multi-channel advertising and direct marketing.
- Government business: U.S. federal government is a significant customer via CMS and federal employee programs; Health Care Benefits revenues from the federal government were 14% in 2022 and 2021 (13% in 2020); CMS Medicare contracts represented ~74%, 79%, and 78% of federal government revenues in 2022, 2021, and 2020, respectively; not dependent on any single non-CMS customer or broker.
- Pricing: Commercial Insured contracts typically set one-year terms with fixed premiums determined at policy start; ASC fees generally fixed for one year; inability to recover unexpected cost increases within the period, with prior experience informing future rates; premium rates filed and approved by states where required.

nodes.title: Health Care Benefits Customers
nodes.heading: 4.5 Health Care Benefits Customers
nodes.start_phrase: Medical membership is dispersed throughout the United States, and the Company also serves medical members in certain countries outside the United States.
nodes.summary:
- Mission and member focus: Support members across their health journey with high service levels, drive healthier outcomes, and prompt next best actions.
- Customer base and reach: Medical membership spans the U.S. with some international coverage; customers include employers, individuals, students, part-time/hourly workers, health plans, providers, government entities, government-sponsored plans, labor groups, and expatriates.
- Product portfolio: Broad range of traditional, voluntary, and consumer-directed health insurance products and related services, available nationwide; offerings include Commercial Insured and Administrative Services Contract (ASC) products.
- Public and private exchanges: Entered individual Public Exchanges in eight states in January 2022 and four additional states in January 2023; also participates in Private Exchanges.
- Medicare/Medicaid: Provides Insured Medicare coverage to individuals and retirees via employer groups; enrolls Medicaid and CHIP members individually; serves dual-eligible (Medicare and Medicaid) members.
- Sales and distribution: Utilizes company sales teams, independent brokers/agents/consultants, and Insurance Exchanges; may pay commissions/fees and can facilitate broker compensation on behalf of customers; marketing includes advertising (TV, radio, billboards, print, social), market research, and direct marketing.
- Employer plan dynamics: Large employers often offer multiple plan options during annual open enrollment; employers typically pay premiums and recoup a portion via employee payroll deductions; some products are fully employee-funded or billed directly to individuals.
- Government exposure and concentration: The U.S. federal government, primarily via CMS for Medicare, is a significant customer; Health Care Benefits segment revenues from the federal government were 14% (2022, 2021) and 13% (2020) of consolidated revenues, with CMS contracts comprising ~74%, 79%, and 78% of those federal revenues, respectively; no material dependence on any single non-government customer or few brokers.
- Pricing and contracts: Commercial Insured contracts typically last one year with fixed premiums set at the start; unexpected cost increases generally cannot be recovered within the period, though past experience informs future pricing; ASC fees are usually fixed for one year; premium rates filed and approved where required by state law.

nodes.title: Health Care Benefits Pricing
nodes.heading: 4.6 Health Care Benefits Pricing
nodes.start_phrase: For Commercial Insured plans, contracts containing the pricing and other terms of the relationship are generally established in advance of the policy period and typically have a duration of one year.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and mission: Health Care Benefits segment focused on high service levels, healthier outcomes, and driving next-best health actions.
- Membership and reach: Medical membership across the U.S. and select international markets.
- Customer segments: Employer groups, individuals, students, part-time/hourly workers, health plans, providers, government units/programs, labor groups, expatriates, and dually eligible members.
- Product portfolio: Traditional, voluntary, and consumer-directed plans; Commercial Insured and ASC arrangements; HMO/PPO; Medicare Advantage, PDP, Medicare Supplement; Medicaid/CHIP; Duals; federal employee dental/vision and medical plans.
- Exchanges: Participation in Public Exchanges began in eight states in 2022 and expanded to four more in 2023; sales also via Private Exchanges.
- Distribution and marketing: Company sales force plus independent brokers/agents/consultants; employer open enrollment processes; direct-to-member billing in some cases; advertising across media and direct marketing; broker/consultant compensation and pass-through arrangements.
- Government business concentration: Federal government is a significant customer via CMS and federal employee programs; 14%, 14%, and 13% of consolidated revenues in 2022–2020 from the federal government, with 74%–79% of that tied to CMS Medicare contracts; not dependent on any single non-government customer or broker.
- Commercial pricing: One-year contracts; fixed premiums set before the policy period with limited ability to recover unexpected costs within the year; state rate filings/approvals can affect timing and levels of premiums.
- ASC pricing: Administrative fees generally fixed for one year.
- Medicare pricing and risk: CMS capitation/premiums adjusted for demographics and risk; PDP risk-sharing; subject to audits and retro/prospective adjustments; supplemental premiums may apply; higher PMPM revenue and costs than commercial lines.
- Star ratings impact: ACA ties Medicare Advantage bonus payments to star ratings ≥4; company’s members in ≥4-star plans declined from 87% (2022 ratings) to 21% (2023 ratings), affecting 2024 bonus eligibility.
- Medicare Supplement: State-regulated rates vary by state and plan.
- Medicaid/CHIP: State-paid fixed PMPM rates (actuarially sound); ASC Medicaid contracts may include performance incentives and limited risk sharing; funding subject to state appropriations.
- Duals: Rates set by CMS with states; potential refunds if requirements aren’t met.
- Federal employee programs: FEHB and FEDVIP rates/fees subject to federal review and audit with possible retro/prospective adjustments and refunds.
- ACA fees and taxes: Industry fees (including the HIF) began in 2014; HIF repealed after 2020; company seeks to price to cover ACA-related assessments.

nodes.title: Health Care Benefits Seasonality
nodes.heading: 4.7 Health Care Benefits Seasonality
nodes.start_phrase: The Health Care Benefits segment’s quarterly operating income progression is impacted by (i) the seasonality of benefit costs which generally increase during the year as Insured members progress through their annual deductibles and out-of-pocket expense limits and (ii) the seasonality of operating expenses,
nodes.summary:
- Explains seasonality in the Health Care Benefits segment’s operating income: benefit costs typically rise over the year as members meet deductibles and out-of-pocket limits, while operating expenses peak in Q4 due to plan-year readiness and Medicare annual enrollment marketing.
- Notes that in 2022, COVID-19 impacts stabilized as related medical costs were incorporated into pricing, restoring a more normal seasonality pattern.
- Details 2021 deviations from typical seasonality: Q1 saw elevated COVID-19 testing and treatment costs and lower Medicare risk-adjusted revenue; Q2 COVID costs persisted but at lower levels; Q3 and Q4 costs rose again with new variants.
- Describes 2020 impacts: sharp decline in discretionary utilization and elective procedures beginning mid-March; gradual recovery in May–June; near-normal utilization in Q3–Q4 with regional COVID waves.
- Outlines a highly competitive health care benefits landscape driven by numerous for-profit and not-for-profit players, new entrants, industry consolidation, and a shift to a consumer-focused retail marketplace with Insurance Exchanges and increased digital engagement.
- Identifies key competitive differentiators: perceived quality and accreditation, service quality, coverage breadth, cost structure (premiums, provider discounts, member cost share), product design, financial strength and ratings, provider network breadth and quality, network option variety, provider availability, and member support and care management.
- States the company believes it competes effectively on these factors; acknowledges competition can influence provider service availability.
- Lists competitors for insured products: local/regional plans, large national insurers, health system-owned plans, Blue Cross Blue Shield licensees; notes Original Medicare as the largest competitor in Medicare.
- Highlights additional competitors: medical and dental provider organizations, specialty service providers including PBMs, consultants, financial services firms, integrated delivery systems assuming risk, TPAs, health IT companies, and certain government programs.
- Notes emerging competition from startup plans, technology companies, provider-owned plans, cross-industry joint ventures (including not-for-profit), and financial and consulting firms distributing products via proprietary Private Exchanges.

nodes.title: Health Care Benefits Competition
nodes.heading: 4.8 Health Care Benefits Competition
nodes.start_phrase: The health care benefits industry is highly competitive, primarily due to a large number of for-profit and not-for-profit competitors, competitors’ marketing and pricing and a proliferation of competing products, including new products that are continually being introduced into the marketplace.
nodes.summary:
- Explains seasonality in Health Care Benefits operating income: benefit costs rise through the year as members meet deductibles/out-of-pocket limits; operating expenses peak in Q4 due to plan-year readiness and Medicare annual enrollment.
- Describes COVID-19 impacts by year:
  - 2022: Stabilized; pricing captured COVID-related costs; return to normal seasonality.
  - 2021: Disrupted seasonality; Q1 higher testing/treatment costs and lower Medicare risk-adjusted revenue; Q2 COVID costs persisted but lower; Q3–Q4 costs rose with new variants.
  - 2020: Sharp drop in discretionary utilization and elective procedures from mid-March; recovery by May–June; more normal levels in Q3–Q4 with regional waves.
- Details a highly competitive Health Care Benefits landscape driven by numerous for-profit and not-for-profit players, new entrants, consolidation, consumer-focused retail shifts (including Insurance Exchanges), and greater technology use.
- Identifies key competitive differentiators: quality and accreditation, service, coverage breadth, cost (premiums, discounts, member cost sharing), product design, financial strength/ratings, network breadth/quality/options, provider availability, and member support/care management; notes the company’s competitiveness on these factors.
- Outlines competitor types: local/regional plans, large national insurers, Blue Cross/Blue Shield licensees, health system-owned plans, provider organizations, specialty providers (including PBMs), consultants, financial services firms, integrated delivery systems, TPAs, HIT companies, and government programs; Original Medicare is the largest Medicare competitor.
- Highlights emerging competitors: startups, technology firms, provider-owned plans, multi-industry joint ventures (including not-for-profit), financial and consulting firms with Private Exchanges, and retail companies; employer self-funding choices also impact insured enrollment.
- Notes ASC plans primarily compete with large commercial insurers, Blue licensees, and TPAs.
- Describes rapid evolution and intense competition in provider solutions and health IT, with many IT competitors holding stronger brands and innovation track records.
- Points to macroeconomic risks: adverse economic conditions and workforce reductions can reduce medical membership.
- Summarizes reinsurance strategy: multiple non-affiliated reinsurance agreements to mitigate catastrophic loss risk and reduce capital/surplus needs; ongoing evaluation and refinement of reinsurance and risk management.
- Introduces Pharmacy Services segment scope: comprehensive PBM solutions (plan design/administration, formulary, retail network, mail order), specialty pharmacy and infusion, clinical and disease management, medical spend management, 340B administration, and services to manufacturers; operates a GPO and diverse dispensing/infusion sites; managed 2.3 billion 30-day equivalent prescriptions in 2022.
- Describes PBM operations: dispensing via mail and retail networks; proprietary systems enable benefit use and automated checks for eligibility, refills, duplicates, dosage, interactions/allergies, overuse, and fraud.
- Explains plan design and administration support: helps clients optimize outcomes and costs; monitors performance through communications, software, and periodic reviews; administers coverage and claims, including services for 340B Covered Entities.

nodes.title: Health Care Benefits Reinsurance
nodes.heading: 4.9 Health Care Benefits Reinsurance
nodes.start_phrase: The Company currently has several reinsurance agreements with non-affiliated insurers that relate to Health Care Benefits insurance policies.
nodes.summary:
- Competitive landscape: The Health Care Benefits segment faces competition from large commercial health insurers, Blue Cross Blue Shield licensees, and third-party administrators (TPAs). In provider solutions and health IT (HIT), it competes with other health plans and specialized IT firms that often have stronger brands and longer operating histories.
- Enrollment drivers and risks: Growth in insured commercial medical enrollment is influenced by employers’ preference and capacity to self-fund. Overall medical membership can be negatively affected by adverse or uncertain economic conditions and employer workforce reductions, particularly in the U.S.
- Reinsurance strategy: The company uses reinsurance with non-affiliated insurers to reduce catastrophic loss exposure and related capital/surplus needs, and it regularly reassesses reinsurance and risk management strategies.
- Pharmacy Services (PBM) scope: Offers comprehensive PBM solutions, including plan design and administration, formulary management, retail network management, and mail order pharmacy. Provides specialty pharmacy, infusion and enteral nutrition services, clinical and disease management, medical spend management, and administrative services for providers and 340B Covered Entities. Operates a group purchasing organization negotiating drug pricing and rebates, and offers administrative, management, and reporting services to pharmaceutical manufacturers.
- Clients and scale: Serves employers, insurers, unions, government employee groups, health plans, PDPs, Managed Medicaid plans, Insurance Exchange plans, and 340B Covered Entities. Operates retail specialty pharmacies, specialty mail order, mail dispensing, compounding pharmacies, and infusion branches. Managed or filled 2.3 billion 30-day equivalent prescriptions in 2022.
- PBM operations and technology: Dispenses via mail order and a retail network. Uses proprietary prescription management systems to support member benefit utilization and automate pharmacist reviews for eligibility, early refills, duplicate dispensing, dosing appropriateness, interactions/allergies, over-utilization, and potential fraud.
- Plan design and administration: Assists clients in designing cost-effective, outcome-focused pharmacy benefits; monitors performance through ongoing communications, proprietary tools, and periodic reviews (annual/quarterly/monthly); administers coverage and claims processing, including administrative services for Covered Entities.

nodes.title: Pharmacy Services Segment
nodes.heading: 5 Pharmacy Services Segment
nodes.start_phrase: The Pharmacy Services segment provides a full range of PBM solutions, including plan design offerings and administration, formulary management, retail pharmacy network management services and mail order pharmacy.
nodes.summary: The excerpt outlines competitive dynamics, risk mitigation, and service offerings across the company’s Health Care Benefits and Pharmacy Services segments. In Health Care Benefits, enrollment growth in insured commercial products is influenced by employers’ preference for self-funding, intense competition from large national insurers, Blue Cross Blue Shield affiliates, and third-party administrators (TPAs), and macroeconomic headwinds that can reduce client workforces and membership. The provider solutions and health IT markets are rapidly evolving, with competition from major health plans and established technology firms with stronger brands and innovation track records. To manage risk, the company uses reinsurance agreements with unaffiliated insurers to limit catastrophic losses and associated capital needs, and it regularly reassesses these strategies. The Pharmacy Services segment delivers end-to-end PBM solutions—plan design, administration, formulary and network management, mail and specialty pharmacy, infusion, clinical and disease management, medical spend management, and 340B administrative services—supported by a group purchasing organization and services for drug manufacturers. Clients span employers, insurers, unions, government groups, health plans (including PDPs and Managed Medicaid), exchange plans, and Covered Entities. Proprietary systems power dispensing and safety checks, while plan performance is monitored via software, frequent communications, and periodic reviews.

nodes.title: Pharmacy Services Segment - Introduction
nodes.heading: 5 Pharmacy Services Segment
nodes.start_phrase: The Pharmacy Services segment provides a full range of PBM solutions, including plan design offerings and administration, formulary management, retail pharmacy network management services and mail order pharmacy.
nodes.summary: Overview of the Company’s Pharmacy Services segment, which delivers comprehensive PBM solutions including plan design and administration, formulary management, retail pharmacy network management, and mail order pharmacy, plus specialty pharmacy, infusion, clinical and disease management, medical spend management, and administrative services for providers and 340B Covered Entities. It operates a group purchasing organization negotiating pharmaceutical pricing and rebates, and provides administrative, management, and reporting services to manufacturers. Clients include employers, insurers, unions, government employee groups, health plans, PDPs, Managed Medicaid plans, Insurance Exchange plans, other plan sponsors, and Covered Entities. Operations span retail specialty pharmacies, specialty mail order, mail order dispensing, compounding pharmacies, and infusion/enteral nutrition branches. In 2022, the PBM filled or managed 2.3 billion 30-day equivalent prescriptions.

nodes.title: PBM Services
nodes.heading: 5.1 PBM Services
nodes.start_phrase: The Company dispenses prescription drugs directly through its mail order dispensing and specialty mail order pharmacies and through pharmacies in its retail network.
nodes.summary:
- Health Care Benefits competition: Administrative services contract (ASC) plans compete with large commercial insurers, Blue Cross/Blue Shield-affiliated organizations, and third-party administrators; provider solutions and health IT (HIT) face rapid market evolution and strong competition from large health plans and specialized IT firms with greater brand recognition and experience. Enrollment is influenced by employers’ propensity to self-fund and by adverse/uncertain economic conditions and workforce reductions.

- Reinsurance: The company uses multiple reinsurance agreements with non-affiliated insurers to mitigate catastrophic loss risk and reduce capital/surplus requirements, and it regularly evaluates and refines its reinsurance strategy.

- Pharmacy Services segment overview: Provides comprehensive PBM solutions (plan design, administration, formulary management, retail network management, mail order), specialty pharmacy and infusion, clinical and disease management, medical spend management, and administrative services for providers and 340B Covered Entities. Operates a group purchasing organization negotiating drug pricing and rebates; offers administrative, management, and reporting services to pharmaceutical manufacturers. Clients include employers, insurers, unions, government groups, health plans, PDPs, Managed Medicaid plans, Exchange plans, and other plan sponsors, plus Covered Entities. Operates multiple dispensing and specialty facilities; managed 2.3 billion 30‑day equivalent prescriptions in 2022.

- PBM operations and technology: Dispenses through mail order, specialty mail order, and a retail network. Proprietary prescription management systems process all claims and support member benefit use while automating checks for eligibility, early refills, duplicates, dosing appropriateness, drug interactions/allergies, over‑utilization, and potential fraud.

- Plan design and administration: Assists clients in designing pharmacy benefits to improve outcomes and control costs; monitors performance via frequent communications, proprietary tools, and periodic reviews (annual/quarterly/monthly). Administers pharmacy benefit plans and provides administrative services to 340B Covered Entities.

nodes.title: Plan Design Offerings and Administration
nodes.heading: 5.2 Plan Design Offerings and Administration
nodes.start_phrase: The Company assists its PBM clients in designing pharmacy benefit plans that help improve health outcomes while minimizing the costs to the client.
nodes.summary:
- Competitive dynamics in Health Care Benefits: pressure from large national insurers, Blue Cross/Blue Shield-affiliated plans, and TPAs; provider solutions/HIT competition from health plans and specialized IT firms with strong brands and innovation track records; insured commercial enrollment influenced by employers’ shift to self-funding; membership sensitive to economic downturns and client workforce reductions.
- Health Care Benefits reinsurance: multiple agreements with non-affiliated insurers to mitigate catastrophic risk and capital requirements; ongoing evaluation and refinement of reinsurance and risk strategies.
- Pharmacy Services (PBM) overview: comprehensive solutions including plan design/administration, formulary management, retail network management, mail order, specialty pharmacy and infusion, clinical and disease management, medical spend management, and services for 340B Covered Entities and providers.
- Group purchasing and manufacturer services: operates a GPO to negotiate drug pricing and rebates; provides administrative, management, and reporting services to pharmaceutical manufacturers.
- Client base and scale: serves employers, insurers, unions, government groups, health plans, PDPs, Managed Medicaid plans, Exchange plans, and 340B Covered Entities; operates retail specialty stores, specialty mail order, compounding pharmacies, and infusion/enteral branches; managed 2.3 billion 30‑day equivalent prescriptions in 2022.
- Technology and claims processing: proprietary prescription management systems support eligibility checks, utilization safeguards (e.g., early refills, duplicates, dosage, interactions, allergies, over‑utilization), and fraud detection across mail and retail channels.
- Plan design support and administration: consults on benefit designs to improve outcomes and lower costs (e.g., promoting generics, tiered formularies); provides performance reviews (annual/quarterly/monthly) and real‑time benefits information at prescribing, in CVS pharmacies, and to members.
- Formulary management: independent CVS Caremark National Pharmacy & Therapeutics Committee governs drug selection based on safety/efficacy and net cost; ongoing drug reviews; many clients adopt template formularies.
- Retail network management: nationwide network of ~66,000 pharmacies (about 40,000 chain, including CVS, and ~26,000 independent) across the U.S. and territories; real‑time POS adjudication integrates with clinical and payment verification.
- Mail order services: maintenance medication fulfillment with pharmacist review that may include generic substitution or therapeutic interchange; URAC Mail Service Pharmacy accreditation.
- Specialty pharmacy and infusion: specialty mail order and retail specialty operations plus infusion/enteral services; accreditations from URAC (Specialty), The Joint Commission, and ACHC, including PCAB for compounding standards.
- Clinical programs: utilization management, medication management, quality assurance, adherence, and counseling to improve outcomes and control pharmacy/medical spend; opioid management program limiting initial acute prescriptions (7‑day supply), capping daily dosages, and preferring immediate‑release before extended‑release; pharmacist counseling via the Pharmacy Advisor program.

nodes.title: Formulary Management
nodes.heading: 5.3 Formulary Management
nodes.start_phrase: The Company utilizes an independent panel of doctors, pharmacists and other medical experts, referred to as the CVS Caremark National Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee, to review and approve the selection of drugs that meet the Company’s standards of safety and efficacy for inclusion on one of the Company’s template formularies.
nodes.summary:
- Recommends pharmacy benefit plan designs that promote clinically appropriate, lower-cost therapy, especially the use of generics; supports tiered member cost-sharing to steer to lower-cost alternatives via formularies.
- Formulary management led by the independent CVS Caremark National Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee, selecting drugs based on safety and efficacy; template formularies aim for member access and lowest net cost; ongoing, independent drug reviews; real-time benefit information delivered at prescribing, at CVS pharmacies, and directly to members.
- Retail pharmacy network management across ~66,000 U.S. pharmacies (about 40,000 chain, including CVS, and 26,000 independent) with point-of-sale integration for eligibility verification, drug utilization review, and payment confirmation.
- Mail order pharmacy services for maintenance medications with pharmacist review, prescriber outreach, generic substitution and therapeutic interchange to reduce cost and improve quality; URAC Mail Service Pharmacy accreditation.
- Specialty pharmacy and infusion/enteral services delivering advanced therapies for chronic/genetic conditions via specialty mail order and retail locations; accreditations include URAC Specialty, The Joint Commission, ACHC, and pharmacy compounding (PCAB under ACHC).
- Clinical programs to improve outcomes and manage costs: utilization management, medication management, quality assurance, adherence, and counseling; opioid management policy limiting initial acute prescriptions to seven days, capping daily dosage, and requiring immediate-release prior to extended-release; Pharmacy Advisor program offering pharmacist counseling in person and by phone.

nodes.title: Retail Pharmacy Network Management Services
nodes.heading: 5.4 Retail Pharmacy Network Management Services
nodes.start_phrase: The Company maintains a national network of approximately 66,000 retail pharmacies, consisting of approximately 40,000 chain pharmacies (which include CVS pharmacy locations) and approximately 26,000 independent pharmacies, in the United States, including Puerto Rico, the District of Columbia, Guam and the U.S. Virgin Islands.
nodes.summary:
- Recommends pharmacy benefit plan designs that prioritize lower-cost, clinically appropriate drugs, encourage use of generics, and leverage tiered member cost-sharing via formularies; provides real-time benefit information at prescribing, in CVS pharmacies, and to members.
- Formulary management overseen by the independent CVS Caremark National Pharmacy & Therapeutics Committee; template formularies with clinically appropriate alternatives aimed at lowest net cost; continuous, independent drug reviews including generics; broad client adoption of template formularies.
- Retail pharmacy network management with a national network of ~66,000 pharmacies (about 40,000 chain including CVS and 26,000 independent) across the U.S., Puerto Rico, D.C., Guam, and the U.S. Virgin Islands; point-of-sale data integrated into proprietary systems for eligibility verification, drug utilization review, and payment confirmation.
- Mail order pharmacy services focused on maintenance medications; pharmacist review supported by prescription management systems; prescriber communications enabling generic substitution or therapeutic interchange when approved; URAC Mail Service Pharmacy accreditation.
- Specialty pharmacy and infusion services including specialty mail order, retail specialty locations, and infusion/enteral nutrition branches; delivery of advanced therapies for chronic/genetic conditions; accreditations include URAC Specialty Pharmacy, The Joint Commission, and ACHC, with compounding standards certified via the Pharmacy Compounding Accreditation Board.
- Clinical services to improve outcomes and manage costs: utilization management, medication management, quality assurance, adherence, and counseling programs; opioid management program limiting initial acute prescriptions to seven days, capping daily dosage, and requiring immediate-release before extended-release; Pharmacy Advisor program enabling pharmacist counseling in person and by phone.

nodes.title: Mail Order Pharmacy Services
nodes.heading: 5.5 Mail Order Pharmacy Services
nodes.start_phrase: The Pharmacy Services segment operates mail order dispensing pharmacies in the United States.
nodes.summary:
- Recommends pharmacy benefit plan designs that prioritize clinically appropriate, lower-cost therapy, especially generics, using tiered member cost sharing and formularies to drive savings.
- Manages formularies through an independent Pharmacy & Therapeutics Committee that selects safe, effective drugs; offers template formularies to balance member access with lowest net cost and conducts ongoing drug reviews.
- Provides real-time benefits information aligned to a member’s plan at e-prescribing, in CVS pharmacies, and directly to members.
- Operates a national retail pharmacy network of about 66,000 pharmacies (chain and independent) with systems for eligibility verification, drug utilization review, and electronic claims/payment confirmation.
- Runs mail order pharmacies focused on maintenance medications, enabling pharmacist review, generic substitution, and therapeutic interchange; accredited by URAC for Mail Service Pharmacy.
- Delivers specialty pharmacy and infusion/enteral nutrition services via specialty mail and retail sites and infusion branches for complex, chronic conditions; holds URAC Specialty accreditation plus Joint Commission and ACHC (including PCAB) accreditations.
- Offers clinical programs—utilization management, medication management, quality assurance, adherence, and counseling—to improve outcomes and control costs.
- Implements opioid management policies limiting initial acute prescriptions (e.g., seven-day supply, dosage limits, immediate-release before extended-release) and provides pharmacist counseling through the Pharmacy Advisor program.

nodes.title: Specialty Pharmacy and Infusion Services
nodes.heading: 5.6 Specialty Pharmacy and Infusion Services
nodes.start_phrase: The Pharmacy Services segment operates specialty mail order pharmacies, retail specialty pharmacy stores and branches for infusion and enteral nutrition services in the United States.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on helping PBM clients design benefit plans that steer members to lower-cost, clinically appropriate drugs, especially generics, using formulary tiers and differential member cost-sharing.
- Formulary management led by an independent P&T Committee (CVS Caremark), with ongoing clinical reviews to ensure safety, efficacy, and lowest net cost; many clients adopt template formularies. Real-time benefit information is provided at prescribing, at CVS pharmacies, and directly to members.
- Retail pharmacy network management across a national network of ~66,000 pharmacies (about 40,000 chain, including CVS, and 26,000 independent) in the U.S. and territories; electronic claims processing includes eligibility checks, drug utilization review, and payment confirmation.
- Mail order pharmacy services for maintenance medications, with pharmacist review supported by proprietary systems; capabilities include generic substitution and therapeutic interchange (with prescriber approval). Mail service pharmacies hold URAC accreditation.
- Specialty pharmacy and infusion services delivered via specialty mail order pharmacies, retail specialty locations, and infusion/enteral nutrition branches for patients with chronic or genetic conditions. Accreditations include URAC, The Joint Commission, and ACHC; compounding accredited by the Pharmacy Compounding Accreditation Board.
- Clinical programs to manage overall pharmacy and medical costs and improve outcomes, including utilization management, medication management, quality assurance, adherence, and counseling programs aligned with client plan designs.
- An opioid-specific UM program that limits initial acute opioid prescriptions for new-to-therapy patients to seven days, caps daily dosages, and requires immediate-release formulations before extended-release products.
- Pharmacy Advisor program enabling pharmacist counseling both in person and by phone to support member adherence and clinical outcomes.

nodes.title: Clinical Services
nodes.heading: 5.7 Clinical Services
nodes.start_phrase: The Company offers multiple clinical programs and services to help clients manage overall pharmacy and health care costs in a clinically appropriate manner.
nodes.summary:
- PBM plan design recommendations to promote lower-cost, clinically appropriate drug use, including encouragement of generics, tiered member cost-sharing, and use of formularies with real-time benefit information at prescribing, pharmacy, and member channels.
- Formulary management led by an independent Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee; template formularies aimed at clinical appropriateness and lowest net cost; ongoing independent drug reviews; broad client adoption.
- Retail pharmacy network management across ~66,000 U.S. pharmacies; real-time claim processing, eligibility verification, drug utilization review, and payment confirmation via proprietary systems.
- Mail order pharmacy services focused on maintenance medications with pharmacist review enabling generic substitution and therapeutic interchange; URAC-accredited mail service pharmacies.
- Specialty pharmacy and infusion/enteral services for complex, chronic, and genetic conditions delivered via specialty mail and retail locations; accreditations from URAC, The Joint Commission, and ACHC/PCAB.
- Clinical services including utilization management, medication management, quality assurance, adherence, and counseling programs; opioid stewardship with limits on initial acute prescriptions; Pharmacy Advisor counseling for chronic conditions; digital tools to surface lower-cost alternatives.
- Disease and care management programs (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, Parkinson’s, epilepsy, multiple sclerosis) with NCQA accreditation; UM programs accredited by NCQA and URAC.
- Medical benefit management through NovoLogix prior authorization to optimize specialty drug use and costs under the medical benefit.
- Group purchasing organization services negotiating pharmaceutical pricing and rebates; administrative and reporting support for manufacturers.
- Information systems: centralized claim adjudication and data platform, Health Engagement Engine, cloud-native and AI-enabled analytics and automation; integrated specialty workflows (e.g., Specialty Expedite) and web platform.
- Client base spanning employers, insurers, unions, government groups, health plans, PDPs, Managed Medicaid, exchange plans, and covered entities; revenue driven by dispensing and managing prescriptions with safety checks and generic opportunities.
- Seasonality: the segment’s revenues are largely non-seasonal.
- Competitive landscape defined by negotiating leverage with manufacturers and pharmacies, effectiveness of clinical cost management and formularies, marketing, service flexibility and responsiveness, product/service quality and cost, and operational excellence amid competition from large national PBMs.

nodes.title: Disease Management Programs
nodes.heading: 5.8 Disease Management Programs
nodes.start_phrase: The Company’s clinical programs and services utilize advanced protocols and offer clients convenience in working with providers and other third parties.
nodes.summary: The excerpt outlines a pharmacy benefit management (PBM) operation focused on improving outcomes and lowering costs for patients with chronic conditions through adherence support, care gap identification, and digital connectivity that surfaces lower-cost drug alternatives via analytics and data sharing. It details accredited clinical programs: disease management for conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, Parkinson’s, epilepsy, and multiple sclerosis (NCQA-accredited) and a utilization management program (NCQA and URAC-accredited). Medical benefit management is delivered through the NovoLogix online preauthorization tool to ensure clinically appropriate use and capture savings for specialty drugs billed under the medical benefit. The Company also runs a group purchasing organization that negotiates pharmaceutical pricing and rebates and provides administrative, management, and reporting services to manufacturers. Its technology stack includes a centralized claim adjudication platform, a Health Engagement Engine with proprietary clinical algorithms, cloud-native and enterprise data capabilities, and assisted AI for insights and automation; specialty services integrate with multiple adjudication platforms and include Specialty Expedite for streamlined onboarding and a new specialty workflow/web platform. Clients span employers, insurers, unions, government employee groups, health plans, PDPs, Managed Medicaid, Exchange plans, and Covered Entities; services include safety checks, drug interaction screening, and generic substitution, with revenues primarily from dispensing and managing prescriptions. Pharmacy Services revenues are largely non-seasonal. Key competitive factors include negotiating leverage with manufacturers and retail networks, effective cost management and formulary strategies, marketing strength, flexible clinically oriented services, quality and cost of offerings, and operational excellence amid competition from numerous national PBMs.

nodes.title: Medical Benefit Management
nodes.heading: 5.9 Medical Benefit Management
nodes.start_phrase: The Company’s NovoLogixonline preauthorization tool helps identify and capture cost savings opportunities for specialty drugs billed under the medical benefit by identifying outliers to appropriate dosages and costs, and helps to ensure clinically appropriate use of specialty drugs.
nodes.summary:

- Disease and utilization management programs use advanced clinical protocols; disease management covers conditions like rheumatoid arthritis, Parkinson’s, epilepsy, and multiple sclerosis; programs are accredited by NCQA (disease management and UM) and URAC (UM).
- Medical benefit management includes the NovoLogix online preauthorization tool to control specialty drug spend under the medical benefit, flag dosage/cost outliers, and ensure clinically appropriate use.
- Group Purchasing Organization services negotiate pharmaceutical pricing and rebates on behalf of participants and provide administrative, management, and reporting services to manufacturers.
- Pharmacy Services information systems feature a centralized claim adjudication platform integrating retail, mail, and specialty; the Health Engagement Engine and clinical algorithms leverage cloud-native tech and assisted AI to drive interventions, automation, and cost/quality improvements; specialty services integrate with adjudication platforms and include Specialty Expedite for onboarding and end-to-end patient management via a new specialty workflow/web platform.
- Client base includes employers, insurers, unions, government employee groups, health plans, PDPs, Managed Medicaid, Exchange plans, and Covered Entities; services encompass safety checks, interaction screening, and generic substitution; revenue is primarily from dispensing/managing prescriptions for members in client plans.
- Pharmacy Services revenues are generally not seasonal.
- Competitive factors include negotiating favorable manufacturer and retail network discounts, effective cost management and preferred formularies, marketing capabilities, flexible clinically oriented client service, breadth/quality/cost of offerings, and operational excellence, in a market with many competitors including large national PBMs.

nodes.title: Pharmacy Services Competition
nodes.heading: 5.14 Pharmacy Services Competition
nodes.start_phrase: The Company believes the primary competitive factors in the pharmacy services industry include: (i) the ability to negotiate favorable discounts from drug manufacturers as well as to negotiate favorable discounts from, and access to, retail pharmacy networks; (ii) the ability to identify and apply effective cost management programs utilizing clinical strategies, including the development and utilization of preferred formularies; (iii) the ability to market PBM products and services; (iv) the commitment to provide flexible, clinically-oriented services to clients and be responsive to clients’ needs; (v) the quality, scope and costs of products and services offered to clients and their members; and (vi) operational excellence in delivering services.
nodes.summary:
- Describes pharmacy benefit management (PBM) capabilities that use digital connectivity, enhanced analytics, and data sharing to lower patient drug costs, support medication adherence, and close care gaps in chronic conditions.

nodes.title: Front Store
nodes.heading: 6.3 Front Store
nodes.start_phrase: Front store revenues reflect the Company’s strategy of innovating with new and unique products and services, using innovative personalized marketing and adjusting the mix of merchandise to match customers’ needs and preferences.
nodes.summary:
- Describes the competitive PBM landscape, noting rivals such as Prime Therapeutics, MedImpact, Express Scripts (Cigna), OptumRx (UnitedHealth), and smaller standalone PBMs.
- Provides an overview of CVS Health’s Retail/LTC segment: retail pharmacies, MinuteClinic services, vaccinations (influenza, COVID-19, shingles), medical diagnostic testing, and long-term care (LTC) pharmacy operations.
- Scale and reach as of December 31, 2022: 9,000+ retail locations, 1,100+ MinuteClinics, online retail pharmacy sites, LTC and on-site pharmacies; 1.6 billion 30-day-equivalent prescriptions filled; approximately 26.8% share of U.S. retail pharmacy prescriptions.
- Product and service mix: prescriptions plus front-store categories (OTC, consumer health, beauty, personal care); participation in the federal 340B program; diversified supplier base; LTC distribution and consulting services.

- Front store strategy: innovation in products/services, personalized marketing, merchandise mix optimization; ExtraCare loyalty program (prices, customized coupons, ExtraBucks rewards); CarePass subscription benefits; proprietary brands (~5,500 SKUs) representing ~21% of 2022 front store revenue.
- MinuteClinic: nurse practitioners and physician assistants deliver guideline-based, convenient, cost-effective care; virtual care offerings; collaboration with Health Care Benefits and Pharmacy Services segments; partnerships with local hospitals and physicians to enhance quality, access, and continuity.

- Medical diagnostic testing delivered via CVS pharmacy sites, MinuteClinics, community-based locations in underserved areas, and the ReturnReady solution.

nodes.summary: The excerpt outlines CVS Health’s Retail/LTC operations, highlighting proprietary brand strategy, care delivery assets, footprint optimization, and technology investments. It notes CVS carries about 5,500 proprietary brand products that generated roughly 21% of front store revenue in 2022. MinuteClinic operated 1,100+ sites staffed by nurse practitioners and physician assistants, offering in-person and virtual care, collaborating with the Health Care Benefits and Pharmacy Services segments, and maintaining relationships with local health systems. CVS also runs a limited number of on-site pharmacies at client locations for prescriptions and vaccinations, including COVID-19, and provides medical diagnostic testing at CVS pharmacies, MinuteClinics, community-based sites in underserved areas, and through its Return Ready solution. Long-term care pharmacy services are delivered via Omnicare to facilities such as skilled nursing and assisted living, with offerings including pharmacy consulting, monthly drug therapy reviews, clinical programs, regulatory support, and pharmaceutical case management for individuals covered under corporate plans. Technology investments include the WeCARE Workflow tool to prioritize pharmacy tasks, support prescriber outreach, and integrate clinical programs, and the Health Engagement Engine with data science algorithms to prompt pharmacist counseling on adherence, care gaps, and chronic condition management—all aimed at enhancing safety, quality, efficiency, and customer experience while lowering costs.

nodes.title: Retail/LTC Information Systems
nodes.heading: 6.9 Retail/LTC Information Systems
nodes.start_phrase: The Company has continued to invest in information systems to enable it to deliver exceptional customer service, enhance safety and quality, and expand patient care services while lowering operating costs.
nodes.summary:
- Emphasis on CVS Health’s Retail/LTC segment, including proprietary brands: ~5,500 private-label products accounting for ~21% of 2022 front store revenue.

nodes.title: Retail/LTC Customers
nodes.heading: 6.10 Retail/LTC Customers
nodes.start_phrase: The success of the Retail/LTC segment’s businesses is dependent upon the Company’s ability to establish and maintain contractual relationships with pharmacy benefit managers and other payors on acceptable terms.
nodes.summary:
- Describes CVS Health’s Retail/LTC digital capabilities that enhance consumer and caregiver experiences, including integrated online and mobile tools for pharmacy navigation and condition management.
- Details the LTC Omniview technology suite, featuring executive dashboards, pre-admission pricing, electronic refill ordering, proof-of-delivery tracking, patient profile access, facility bill management, and real-time Medicare Part D validation.
- Outlines online scheduling infrastructure for diagnostic testing and vaccinations via CVS.com and MinuteClinic.com, including service information, eligibility screening, location/appointment selection, digital registration, reminders (SMS/email), and delivery of digital test results and vaccination records.
- Explains Retail/LTC customer and payor mix: revenues largely from PBMs, MCOs, government programs, employers, and other third-party payors; no single payor accounted for 10%+ of consolidated revenues in 2020–2022.
- Notes seasonality: pharmacy revenues are generally not seasonal; front store sales rise in December; both pharmacy and front store results vary with cough/cold/flu season severity and unusual weather.
- Summarizes COVID-19 impacts on quarterly operating trends:
  - 2022: Strong Q1 vaccinations and OTC test kit sales with the year’s highest diagnostic testing; Q2–Q3 moderation with more in-home testing; Q4 uptick in vaccinations tied to the bivalent booster.
  - 2021: Q1 lower store traffic due to a weak flu season but peak diagnostic testing; Q2 earnings from vaccinations and improved traffic; Q3–Q4 ongoing vaccinations (including boosters), diagnostic testing, and OTC test kit sales.
  - 2020: March surge in prescriptions (90-day fills/early refills) and front store purchases; Q2 onward reduced traffic, fewer new therapy prescriptions, and lower LTC volume; Q3 increase in COVID-19 diagnostic testing; December start of LTC COVID-19 vaccinations.

nodes.title: Retail/LTC Seasonality
nodes.heading: 6.11 Retail/LTC Seasonality
nodes.start_phrase: The majority of Retail/LTC segment revenues, particularly pharmacy revenues, generally are not seasonal in nature.
nodes.summary:
- Describes CVS’s integrated digital and mobile solutions that streamline the consumer pharmacy experience and support condition management.
- Details the Omniview LTC digital suite, including executive dashboards, pre-admission pricing, electronic refill ordering, proof-of-delivery tracking, patient profile access, facility billing management, and real-time Medicare Part D validation.
- Outlines online tools enabling patients to schedule diagnostic tests and vaccinations via CVS.com and MinuteClinic.com, with features such as service information pages, eligibility screening, location/appointment selection, registration, automated SMS/email reminders, and delivery of digital test results and vaccination records.
- Explains Retail/LTC customer and payor mix, noting reliance on PBMs, MCOs, government programs, employers, and other third-party payors, with no single payor representing 10% or more of consolidated revenues from 2020–2022.
- Reviews seasonality, noting generally non-seasonal pharmacy revenues, higher front store sales in December, and sensitivity to cough/cold/flu seasons and extreme weather.
- Summarizes COVID-19 impacts on quarterly operating trends:
  - 2022: High Q1 vaccination volumes and OTC test kit sales amid Omicron; peak Q1 diagnostic testing (below 2021 levels); continued but lower testing/vaccination and OTC kit earnings in Q2–Q3; Q4 increase from bivalent booster vaccinations.
  - 2021: Q1 reduced retail traffic and highest diagnostic testing; Q2 vaccination-driven earnings and traffic recovery; Q3–Q4 ongoing vaccinations (including boosters), diagnostic testing, and OTC test kit sales.
  - 2020: March surge in prescriptions (90-day fills, early refills) and front store purchases; subsequent traffic declines and reduced new therapy and LTC scripts; Q3 ramp-up of diagnostic testing; December start of COVID-19 vaccinations in long-term care facilities.

nodes.title: Retail/LTC Competition
nodes.heading: 6.12 Retail/LTC Competition
nodes.start_phrase: The retail pharmacy business is highly competitive.
nodes.summary:
- Retail/LTC competition: Retail pharmacy competes on location/convenience, service, product selection, and price against drugstore chains (Walgreens, Rite Aid), supermarkets, discount retailers (Walmart), independents, restrictive networks, internet firms (Amazon), membership clubs, clinics, urgent/primary care, and mail order. LTC pharmacy is regional/local with PharMerica as the largest national competitor plus many local/regional and facility-owned pharmacies; “freedom of choice/any willing provider” laws can intensify competition.
- Corporate/Other segment: Captures enterprise management and administrative costs (executive, corporate relations, legal, compliance, HR, IT, finance), transformation and modernization investments, acquisition integration costs, and runoff products (large case pensions and long-term care insurance).
- Generic sourcing venture: 50/50 joint venture with Cardinal Health (Red Oak Sourcing) to source and negotiate generic pharmaceutical contracts for both companies; Red Oak holds no inventory.
- Working capital practices: Growth funded by operating cash flow plus short- and long-term borrowings. Most Health Care Benefits and pharmacy third-party receivables settle in under 30 days; Medicare Part D CMS settlements take several quarters, affecting year-to-year working capital. Retail/LTC non-pharmacy sales are mostly cash/debit/credit; remaining pharmacy revenues also include cash/card payments.
- Human capital: Purpose-driven focus on attracting, developing, and retaining talent with competitive rewards and support for a diverse workforce. Over 300,000 employees as of December 31, 2022, primarily in the U.S. (all states, DC, Puerto Rico), with approximately 73% full-time.

nodes.title: Corporate/Other Segment

LTC pharmacy competition is local/regional, with PharMerica as the largest national competitor; competition also includes regional/institutional and facility-owned pharmacies and local retail pharmacies. State “freedom of choice”/“any willing provider” laws can intensify LTC competition in Medicaid.
- Corporate/Other segment: Includes enterprise management and administrative functions (executive, corporate relations, legal, compliance, HR, IT, finance), transformation and modernization investments, acquisition integration costs, and runoff products (large case pensions and long-term care insurance) for which no new customers are accepted.
- Generic sourcing venture: Red Oak Sourcing, a 50/50 JV with Cardinal Health, consolidates sourcing/negotiation of generic pharmaceutical supply contracts for both companies; it does not hold inventory.
- Working capital practices: Growth funded by operating cash flow, commercial paper, and other short- and long-term borrowings. Most Health Care Benefits receivables (employers, individuals, students, part-time/hourly workers, health plans, providers, government units, government-sponsored plans) settle in under 30 days. Medicare Part D arrangements with CMS create receivables/payables that settle over several quarters, affecting working capital. Retail/LTC non-pharmacy revenues are largely paid via cash/debit/credit. Pharmacy revenues predominantly come from MCOs, PBMs, government programs, employers, and other third-party payers that typically settle in under 30 days; the remainder are cash/debit/credit.
- Human capital: Purpose-driven focus on attracting, developing, and retaining talent with competitive rewards and support for a diverse workforce. Over 300,000 employees as of December 31, 2022, primarily in the U.S. across all states, D.C., and Puerto Rico; approximately 73% full-time.

nodes.title: Generic Sourcing Venture
nodes.heading: 7.1 Generic Sourcing Venture
nodes.start_phrase: The Company and Cardinal Health, Inc. (“Cardinal”) each have a 50% ownership in Red Oak Sourcing, LLC (“Red Oak”), a generic pharmaceutical sourcing entity.
nodes.summary:
- Retail/LTC Competition: Highly competitive retail pharmacy market competing on location/convenience, customer service, product selection, and price. Competitors include national drugstore chains (Walgreens, Rite Aid), supermarkets, discount retailers (Walmart), independent pharmacies, restrictive networks, internet companies (Amazon), membership clubs, clinics, urgent/primary care offices, and mail order pharmacies. LTC pharmacy competition is regional/local with PharMerica as the largest national competitor, plus local/regional institutional and facility-owned pharmacies; “freedom of choice/any willing provider” laws in some states can intensify competition.

- Corporate/Other Segment: Includes enterprise management and administrative functions (executive, corporate relations, legal, compliance, HR, IT, finance), costs for transformation and modernization initiatives, acquisition integration, and legacy products no longer marketed (large case pensions and long-term care insurance).

- Generic Sourcing Venture: Red Oak Sourcing LLC is a 50/50 venture with Cardinal Health to source and negotiate generic pharmaceutical supply contracts for both companies; it leverages combined sourcing/supply chain expertise and does not own or hold inventory.

- Working Capital Practices: Growth funded via operating cash flow, commercial paper, short-term and long-term borrowings. Most Health Care Benefits receivables settle in under 30 days; Medicare Part D arrangements with CMS can take several quarters to settle, affecting working capital. Retail/LTC non-pharmacy revenues are largely paid via cash/debit/credit. Most pharmacy revenues come from third-party payers (MCOs, PBMs, government programs, employers) settling in under 30 days; the remainder are cash/debit/credit.

- Human Capital: Purpose-driven focus on delivering care and investing in talent attraction, development, and retention with competitive rewards. Over 300,000 U.S.-based colleagues as of December 31, 2022, across all states, D.C., and Puerto Rico; approximately 73% full-time.
